story.conflict: A widower must decide how to respond when a family wedding treats his wife's absence as an expense he should have filled with another guest.
story.hook: A bride charged a widower for his dead wife's empty chair. He'd thought the place card was there to remember her.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE WAS MORE THAN A SEAT
story.premise: A bride charges a widower for his late wife's unused wedding meal, after he mistakes her place card for a gesture of remembrance.
story.punchline: The receipt went in the bin.
story.script: Arthur touched the card beside his plate. His wife's name was printed in the same gold letters as his. He thanked his niece for keeping it. She handed him a bill for a hundred and eighty dollars. The caterer had charged for the meal, she said. Arthur reminded her he'd called when Ellen died two weeks before the wedding. The numbers had already been confirmed. His niece said he could have brought somebody else. Arthur looked at the empty chair. She said a friend would have done; she hadn't insisted on another wife. He asked whether she'd kept the card as a memory or as a meal count. She said she had a wedding to pay for. Her father came over and asked Arthur not to make things difficult on her big day. Arthur hadn't raised his voice. He said he was trying to understand what he'd been invited to share. His niece asked whether he was refusing to pay. He took out the money and asked for a receipt. Then he put Ellen's place card in his pocket. When the photographer called the family together, Arthur asked his brother to tell them he'd gone home. His brother said Ellen would have wanted him in the photograph. Arthur said she would have wanted him to be comfortable there. At home, he put the gold-lettered card beside her picture. The receipt went in the bin.
story.twist: The place card he thought honored his wife is being used to justify the charge for her unused meal.

youtube.description: A widower mistakes his wife's wedding place card for a memorial gesture, until the bride presents him with the cost of her empty seat.
youtube.title: The Price Beside Her Place Card

story.conflict: An aunt must keep the children secure while refusing to let their mother's unilateral decision determine everyone's future.
story.hook: Her sister moved abroad and left the children on her doorstep. The children thought their mother was coming back after the weekend.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THE CHILDREN DESERVED A PLAN
story.premise: A woman moves abroad after leaving her two children on her sister's doorstep without asking her to become their permanent caregiver.
story.punchline: the children knew where they were going and who was coming back.
story.script: Anna opened the bags and found school uniforms under the pajamas. Then her sister, Lucy, called from the airport. It wasn't a weekend trip. She'd bought a one-way ticket and said Anna's spare room would be a better home for the children. Anna asked when she'd agreed to raise them. Lucy said family didn't need permission to help family. Anna had an early hospital shift and nobody arranged to watch them. Lucy said she'd work something out. Then she announced boarding and ended the call. Eight-year-old Ben asked whether his mother had forgotten their school shoes. Anna sat beside him and said the adults were sorting things out. She called their father, Mark. Lucy had told him she was taking the children on holiday. He hadn't known about Anna's doorstep or the one-way flight. He arrived with his car seats before bedtime. Lucy called from abroad and accused Anna of sending the children away. Anna said she was speaking to their father, not sending them to strangers. Mark asked Lucy why she'd decided he couldn't have them. She said his flat was too small. He said the children could take his bedroom; he could sleep on the sofa. Then he put the phone down to listen to Ben. Anna helped them pack the uniforms properly. She promised to visit on Sunday. This time, the children knew where they were going and who was coming back.
story.twist: The children's father has not agreed to the move or refused their care; their mother bypassed him along with her sister.

youtube.description: An aunt discovers that a weekend visit was really her sister's plan to move abroad without the children or anyone else's agreement.
youtube.title: School Uniforms Under the Weekend Pajamas

story.conflict: A worker must decide whether to stand by a safety complaint when her manager exposes her identity to discourage the rest of the staff.
story.hook: Her boss publicly named the worker behind an anonymous complaint. She'd asked not to close the shop alone after it had been robbed.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SAFETY WAS EVERYONES CONCERN
story.premise: A manager publicly names the worker behind a promised anonymous complaint about closing the shop alone after a robbery.
story.punchline: It wasn't the only one anymore.
story.script: Nina found her name written above the complaint on the staff noticeboard. Her manager, Gary, had promised the team wouldn't know who'd submitted it. Now he'd pinned it beside the closing rota. He said people deserved to know why their hours might change. Nina asked why he'd promised anonymity if he meant to identify her. Gary said she was the only one who'd made a fuss after the robbery. A coworker, Sal, asked whether that meant he hadn't noticed the rest of them checking the door every few minutes. Gary told her not to encourage Nina. Then he handed Nina a pen and said she could withdraw the complaint before it caused a problem. Nina took the pen. He reached for the noticeboard pin, expecting her to take the page down. She said her request hadn't changed. She still didn't want to be the only person locking up. Gary said everyone had managed before. Sal asked whether he was volunteering to close alone that night. He said that wasn't the point. Sal took the pen from Nina and wrote her own name underneath. Another cashier added his. Gary told them this wasn't how complaints were handled. Nina pointed to the noticeboard he'd chosen. By the end of the shift, four names were on the page. The next closing rota still needed sorting out. Nina left her name at the top. It wasn't the only one anymore.
story.twist: The manager expects identifying one frightened employee to isolate her, but coworkers share the concern he has made personal.

youtube.description: A manager exposes a worker's anonymous safety complaint, expecting her coworkers to turn against her.
youtube.title: The Name Above the Anonymous Complaint

story.conflict: A chef must stop her employer using a false death story to collect money for her family without becoming part of his attempt to explain it away.
story.hook: A chef caught her boss selling tickets to her memorial dinner. Her mother was already getting condolence calls, and she was standing in the kitchen.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF HE HAD TO EXPLAIN IT
story.premise: A living chef discovers her boss selling tickets to her memorial dinner while her mother receives genuine condolence calls.
story.punchline: That was where her family actually needed her.
story.script: Rosa had come to collect her shoes on her day off. Her boss, Victor, told her to stay behind the kitchen door. Her photograph stood surrounded by flowers. A customer was crying beside it. Rosa's phone rang. Her mother asked why a neighbor wanted to know when the funeral was. Rosa said she was alive and at the restaurant. Victor reached for the phone, saying they needed to talk first. She moved away. Her mother stayed on the line. Victor admitted he'd told customers Rosa had died and the dinner would help her family with funeral costs. He'd sold thirty-dollar tickets. Rosa asked why. He said nobody had booked the ordinary dinner that week. This had filled every table. He offered to give her some of the money if she'd let him finish the evening. Rosa asked what story he expected her to tell her mother. He said they could explain it as a misunderstanding. Rosa walked into the dining room with the phone still in her hand. She told the customers she was Rosa, she hadn't died, and her family hadn't asked for a fundraiser. Victor said he'd explain the tickets. She said he could do that himself. Then she took her photograph off the memorial table and left. Outside, she asked her mother whether she wanted her to come over. Her mother said yes. That was where her family actually needed her.
story.twist: The supposed family fundraiser is a scheme to fill the restaurant, while the real family needs reassurance that she is alive.

youtube.description: A living chef walks into a fundraiser for her own funeral and finds her boss has already reached her family with the lie.
youtube.title: Thirty Dollars for Her Memorial Dinner
